description:
We are a student team representing UHRET (Hackathon, Robotics and Electronics Community) at Öztimurlar Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School in Bursa, Türkiye.

Our interests include software development, artificial intelligence, electronics, and space technologies. As part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to combine our technical skills and creativity to develop meaningful solutions while gaining experience in teamwork and scientific problem-solving.
summary:
QK norm is an AI-powered scientific research platform designed to support the development of safer fire detection technologies for spacecraft.

In microgravity, smoke behaves differently than on Earth, making reliable fire detection challenging. NASA and NIST research has documented detection limitations for certain materials, highlighting the need for improved sensing technologies.

To address this challenge, we developed three specialized machine learning modules using NASA experimental data. Model A predicts flame spread rates using BASS-II experiments. Model B analyzes flame-related positions in SAFFIRE-I imagery. Model C uses Random Forest classification and material-based analysis to investigate smoke detection signal thresholds using SAME and SAME-R experiments.

Our platform combines these models with an interactive dashboard, scientific evidence catalog, and AI-assisted research explanations. It helps researchers compare experimental conditions, identify gaps in available evidence, and distinguish model predictions from actual measurements.

Rather than claiming to replace spacecraft fire detectors, QK norm provides transparent, evidence-based decision support to guide future research toward more reliable spacecraft fire detection systems.
details:
QK norm — Project Details

QK norm is an AI-powered scientific research platform developed to support spacecraft fire safety research using real NASA experimental data.

How Does It Work?

In microgravity, smoke and flames behave differently than on Earth, creating challenges for spacecraft fire detection.

To investigate these challenges, we developed three specialized machine learning modules:

  • Model A (BASS-II): Predicts PMMA flame spread rates based on material dimensions, airflow velocity, and initial oxygen concentration.
  • Model B (SAFFIRE-I): Analyzes experimental imagery to estimate the horizontal position of a bright flame-related feature.
  • Model C (SAME/SAME-R): Investigates whether smoke measurement signals reach a defined 2.0 V threshold. We evaluated Random Forest classification against simpler material-based methods.

We also integrated a WT4-based language model, a structured scientific evidence catalog, and an interactive dashboard that connects experimental measurements, predictions, and their scientific context.

Technologies and Development

Our project uses Python, machine learning, image analysis, statistical evaluation, and command-line tools.

We worked with NASA's BASS-II, SAFFIRE-I, SAME, and SAME-R experimental resources.

We evaluated models using cross-validation, baseline comparisons, and appropriate scientific metrics. The platform supports repeatable experiments and displays the limitations of its predictions.

Innovation and Creativity

What makes QK norm different is its combination of multiple specialized scientific AI models with an evidence-based research system.

Beyond generating predictions, our platform includes a Blindspot Discovery capability that identifies gaps in the available scientific evidence and proposes questions for future investigation.

Instead of combining unrelated experiments into an artificial safety score, we preserve their individual conditions, measurements, and scientific limitations.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our platform helps researchers:

  • Analyze NASA fire safety experiments more efficiently.
  • Compare experimental conditions and model predictions.
  • Identify limitations in existing scientific evidence.
  • Prioritize future experiments and research questions.
  • Explore results through an accessible interactive interface.

Our ultimate goal is to accelerate research toward more reliable spacecraft fire detection technologies, contributing to safer future space missions.

QK norm is a research decision-support platform, not a physical fire detector. We explicitly distinguish measured experimental results from AI predictions and do not claim validated operational fire prevention performance.
